Net balance in units. [1]

| Year | Balance (units) |
| --- | --- |
| 2021 | -8 [1] |
| 2022 | 4 [1] |
| 2024 | 12 [1] |

Three observations; no forecast or causal effect was established. [1][2]

citations.quote: Synthetic net balances in units were -8 in 2021, 4 in 2022, and 12 in 2024. The year intervals are one year then two years. The records do not identify what caused the changes.
The three observations are not a forecast. A straight segment between recorded values does not establish an intermediate observation or a constant annual rate.

findings.problem: The Year and Balance columns run together: the 2022 row renders as "20224" and the 2024 row as "2024 12", so readers cannot tell where the year ends and the value begins (and "2021 -8" can read as a subtraction). The table's meaning is broken.
findings.correction: Give the Balance column its own clearly separated x-position (shift it right of the Year column with a visible gap, or add a divider/column rule) and right-align the balance values so each year and its value are unambiguous; no text change needed.

findings.problem: The negative value uses a hyphen and left-aligned numerals, making the sign easy to miss next to the year.
findings.correction: Use a true minus sign (−8) and right-align the Balance column so signs line up vertically.

beforeFindings.problem: Body text is 20.0px; the body floor is 22px.
beforeFindings.correction: Allocate more room and increase type; keep values and qualifications intact.

beforeFindings.problem: The data table is not visible; the rendered chart directly labels only "12 units." The 2021 value "-8 units" and 2022 value "4 units" are missing, and with no y-axis zero/scale the negative value and the "cross zero" claim cannot be read from the chart.
beforeFindings.correction: Render the table in a clear area or label all three points with -8 units, 4 units, and 12 units; add a labeled zero baseline or y-axis values, and keep the uneven 2021-2022-2024 spacing.

beforeFindings.problem: The chart axis title "Balance (units)" is set at about 20pt, below the 22pt minimum, making it the smallest required text on the slide.
beforeFindings.correction: Increase the axis-title type to at least 22pt, or remove it because the subtitle already gives the unit.
